item.research_question: How do the addition of high-melting-point metal elements (V, Mo) and a non-metallic element (B) affect the phase composition, microstructure, mechanical properties, and fracture mechanism of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloys?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 base alloy with additions of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 at.% V, Mo, or B
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting of raw materials (>99.5% purity) with 4 iterations of repeated melting to produce ~80 g ingots, followed by stress relief annealing at 200 °C for 3 h
item.test_conditions: Micro-hardness tested at loads of 100, 200, 300, 500, and 1000 g (15 s dwell); tensile tests on 8 mm × 2 mm × 2 mm samples at a strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹
key_findings: The Mo0.2 alloy achieved the highest tensile strength of 1346.3 MPa and fracture elongation of 24.6%.
All alloys with V and Mo additions exhibited tensile strengths exceeding 1000 MPa.
The hardness of the B0.3 alloy reached HV498.1, which is 48% higher than the base alloy.
The FCC phase proportion decreased and then increased with V and Mo content, while it increased and then decreased with B content.
V and Mo elements were distributed in both dendritic (FCC) and interdendritic (BCC) phases.
The fracture mechanism for V and Mo alloys was mixed ductile and brittle, whereas the B-containing alloy showed cleavage fracture.
The Mo0.2 alloy showed a volume ratio of BCC to FCC phases of 28:72.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the superior properties of the Mo0.2 alloy to the coordination of deformation facilitated by fine microstructures and a high proportion of the FCC phase, which allows for plastic deformation in dendritic lamellae while cracks propagate through the BCC lamellae. For B-containing alloys, the increase in hardness is attributed to grain refinement, an increase in the proportion of the harder BCC phase, and a morphological change from lamellar eutectic to petal-like structures.
quotes: The Mo0.2 alloy had the highest tensile strength, of 1346.3 MPa, and fracture elongation, of 24.6%.
The fracture mechanism of Mo0.2 alloy is mainly crack propagation in the BCC lamellae, and the FCC dendritic lamellae exhibit the characteristics of plastic deformation.
The addition of nonmetallic element B has the most noticeable effect on the hardness.
